Between 2015-16 and 2023-24, Pakistan's national greenhouse-gas emissions increased by 17.1%.

In 2015-16, the national total stood at 401.09 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent (Mt CO2e). By 2023-24, under the reference estimate, emissions had grown to 469.64 Mt CO2e, representing an absolute increase of 68.55 Mt CO2e over the nine-year period. These figures use the IPCC 2013 (AR5) warming potentials.

The dataset does not estimate total emissions across all sectors for calendar years; national totals are calculated only for Pakistan's fiscal years (July to June). 

In 2019-20, Pakistan's total emissions were 446.73 Mt CO2e (using IPCC 2013 AR5 global warming potentials). In the following fiscal year, 2020-21, the national total was 479.51 Mt CO2e. 

The one exception is the agriculture sector, which is also calculated on a calendar-year basis. In 2020, Pakistan's agricultural emissions alone were 193.35 Mt CO2e.
The 2023-24 fiscal year starts on July 1, 2023, and ends on June 30, 2024.

cases.answer_text:
Under IPCC reporting rules, Pakistan's industry fuel combustion emitted 28.13 million tonnes of CO2e in 2023-24.

The IPCC reporting view regroups emissions by where they are burned rather than by economic purpose. This figure combines:
* The general industry sector's fuel combustion (<cite k="1" cell="3" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">22.58</cite> <cite k="1" cell="3" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">Mt CO₂e</cite>).
* Captive power generation by industrial plants (<cite k="1" cell="5" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">5.55</cite> <cite k="1" cell="5" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">Mt CO₂e</cite>), which this inventory models as part of the power sector but the IPCC assigns to industry.

Note that Industrial Processes and Product Use (IPPU) — which covers non-combustion chemical releases like cement calcination — is reported as a separate IPCC sector. It added a further <cite k="1" cell="4" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">25.54</cite> <cite k="1" cell="4" receipt="b7b2d2c251888bc971c269d58e16a82b">Mt CO₂e</cite> in 2023-24.

cases.answer_text:
Under the survey configuration (`S_2023_24`), the dung that is no longer burned by households is simply left without a fate in the inventory model. 

The cross-sector transfer ledger for dung tracks exactly 58.74 million tonnes of air-dry dung cake available from agriculture in 2023-24. Under the reference estimate, all 58.74 million tonnes are transferred to the residential sector. Under the survey configuration, only 11.97 million tonnes are transferred to households, and the remaining 46.77 million tonnes are logged in the ledger as "unresolved" with no destination. 

Because the survey configuration is built to recalculate the residential sector alone, it does not re-allocate that excess dung back into agriculture (such as adding it to manure management or agricultural soils). The unburned portion is simply unaccounted for in this configuration.

The release cannot show the survey-based estimate across all nine years because that configuration exists for 2023-24 only. In 2023-24, Pakistan's total emissions under the survey-based estimate were <cite k="2" cell="0" receipt="c7dd5d0f54de282a36be821822881ec6">464.51</cite> <cite k="2" cell="0" receipt="c7dd5d0f54de282a36be821822881ec6">Mt CO₂e</cite>.

If you would like to see how emissions have changed over time, a nine-year trend is available for the reference estimate. No, that would not be statistically valid, and this dataset does not carry a "fugitive structural alternative". 

You cannot simply add the impact of an alternative method to the top of an uncertainty range. An uncertainty range represents a 95% confidence interval for one specific calculation method, based on the statistical uncertainty of its inputs (parametric uncertainty). A different methodological choice (structural uncertainty) would produce its own point estimate and its own entirely separate probability distribution. Adding an alternative scenario to the upper bound of a reference estimate mixes these two concepts and does not represent a valid or measurable "worst case." 

Additionally, the only alternative configuration included in this release is the survey-based estimate for household demand (`S_2023_24`), which exists for the 2023-24 year. There are no structural alternatives provided for the fugitives sector.
